sentence: Creatinine and eGFR show how well the kidneys filter blood, and kidney disease is confirmed only when abnormal results persist.
note: LTO: creatinine and eGFR move in opposite directions; NHS: diagnosis needs results consistently low over time

sentence: Creatinine is a waste product, and the blood test measures how much of it is in the blood.
note: NHS 111 Wales: waste product creatinine in your blood

sentence: The eGFR, or estimated glomerular filtration rate, is calculated from the creatinine result.
The calculation also takes account of age and sex.
note: LTO (blended summary): CKD-EPI equation uses creatinine, age and sex

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK explains that the eGFR may fall over time as kidney function declines.
Because eGFR comes from a routine blood test, it lets clinicians spot kidney problems before symptoms appear.
People with more muscle naturally make more creatinine, which can give a lower eGFR than their kidney function really is.
note: added after second pass: third-pass supported: NICE: more muscle produces more creatinine, giving lower eGFR than true function.

sentence: Cystatin C is another marker filtered by the kidneys and is less affected by muscle mass than creatinine.
note: added after second pass: third-pass supported: Cystatin C less affected by muscle mass than creatinine (NICE; cohort study).

sentence: A low eGFR may be a sign of kidney disease, though a single result is not enough to say.
note: NIDDK: eGFR below a threshold is one sign of decreased kidney function | edited after second pass

sentence: NICE says testing for chronic kidney disease uses both an eGFR and a urine ACR.
note: NIDDK clinical guidance | edited after second pass

sentence: A slightly raised urine ACR, which checks for the protein albumin, may indicate early-stage kidney disease.
eGFR falls naturally with age, which does not always mean kidney disease.
The estimate is unreliable when kidney function is changing quickly, as in acute kidney injury.
One abnormal result is not enough.
A diagnosis is usually confirmed only if repeated eGFR tests are consistently lower than normal over about three months.
NICE says a low first eGFR should be repeated soon, to check whether sudden kidney injury is the cause.
note: PMC6058619 abstract (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: The urine albumin to creatinine ratio, or ACR, compares albumin with creatinine in a urine sample.
Alongside the eGFR, urine tests give a more accurate picture of how well the kidneys are working.
Results are classed by eGFR category and by ACR category, which together show the stage.
Lab Tests Online UK says a very high urine ACR shows that kidney disease is present in a more severe form.
note: added after second pass: third-pass edited: Lab Tests Online UK says very high ACR shows more severe kidney disease; 'very low means normal' per NHS not seen.

sentence: Testing is recommended for people with risk factors such as diabetes, high blood pressure, past acute kidney injury or cardiovascular disease.
Early chronic kidney disease often causes no symptoms, so it is commonly found through routine blood or urine tests.
Later symptoms can include tiredness, swollen ankles, feet or hands, shortness of breath, blood in the urine and passing urine more often at night.
The NHS advises seeing a GP about symptoms that persist.
Creatinine-based eGFR may be less reliable in older adults.
In that situation another marker, cystatin C, can help.
Creatinine can also be influenced by factors other than the kidneys, such as how much muscle a person has.
note: author wording; second pass to confirm | edited after second pass

sentence: NICE advises that the urine ACR is ideally measured on an early morning sample.
note: added after second pass: third-pass supported: NICE recommends ACR ideally on an early morning sample.

sentence: Chronic kidney disease is most often caused by damage from other conditions, most commonly diabetes and high blood pressure.
There is no cure, but care can slow progression.
Kidney function is monitored with regular blood and urine tests.
Care centres on blood pressure control, managing diabetes, prescribed medicines, diet advice and not smoking.
The NHS says medicines can help control related problems and keep the kidneys working for longer.
note: blended summary | edited after second pass

sentence: The NHS says most people with chronic kidney disease can control the condition with medicine and regular check-ups.
note: added after second pass: third-pass supported: NHS: most people with CKD manage it with medicine and regular check-ups.

sentence: Glomerulonephritis, inflammation of the filters inside the kidneys, is another cause of kidney disease.
note: added after second pass: third-pass supported: NHS lists glomerulonephritis (kidney inflammation) among causes of CKD.

sentence: NICE guideline NG203 says the monitoring frequency it recommends is a minimum, and that more frequent monitoring may suit some people.
NICE sets a minimum number of checks each year, which depends on the eGFR and ACR categories.
note: NICE (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: It also reflects how quickly the eGFR or ACR is changing and other conditions such as diabetes.
NICE says ACR monitoring should be individualised, for example more often when the ACR is higher.
NICE lists diabetes among the risk factors for which eGFR and ACR testing is advised.
Creatinine is a waste product measured in the blood, and eGFR is an estimate of kidney filtering worked out from it.
As kidney function declines, the eGFR may fall over time.
One abnormal result is not enough to diagnose chronic kidney disease, which is confirmed when eGFR stays low over about three months.
A urine test, the albumin to creatinine ratio, is used alongside eGFR because it can show kidney damage.
